payload.rationale: YES requires at least four distinct Atlantic hurricanes reaching Category 3 or higher during the specified January 1–December 1, 2026 window; landfall is not required. With no supplied observations or seasonal outlook, I use a climatological judgment: modern Atlantic seasons average roughly three major hurricanes, with substantial year-to-year variability. Four or more is therefore a meaningful but less-than-even possibility, estimated at 40%. This is a full-season estimate, not the probability of four additional major hurricanes after September 19. Although much of the season has elapsed, the absence of reported storms here does not imply that none occurred. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that 2026 may already have had a quiet peak season, leaving insufficient activity before the deadline. The strongest reason it could be too low is that several qualifying hurricanes—or even all four required—may already have occurred. Favorable late-season conditions could also raise the probability.
limitations: No 2026 hurricane counts, storm histories, or current seasonal forecasts were supplied.
The estimate cannot incorporate the highly informative season-to-date record as of the information cutoff.
Climatology is a transfer assumption, not an observation of 2026 conditions.
No additional frozen contract provisions were supplied beyond the event definition.
